master.title: Stability analysis of a novel on-orbit propellant storage and transfer system
master.content:
The interest in interplanetary space travel has been surfacing in the recent times and the technology associated with long distance space missions has been evolving. One of the main concerns for space vehicles traveling beyond Low Earth orbit (LEO) is the requirement of large amounts of propellant. Large amounts of liquid propellant are not only required to escape the gravitational bounds of the earth but also to produce a large enough ΔV to allow the spacecraft to obtain orbital velocities required for geosynchronous and transfer orbits. On-orbit refueling has been identified by as a critical technology for space exploration. Current in-space propellant transfer concepts rely on expensive and heavy pumps that may not guarantee high transfer efficiency or reliability. Researchers at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University in collaboration with Florida Institute of Technology (FIT), have devised an innovative on-orbit propellant transfer concept that uses the spinning of tanks to achieve the propellant transfer by rotational fluid settling. This paper covers the stability analysis of the rotating propellant depot system. Simple analytical models are developed to answer key questions on the stability boundaries of the propellant transfer model. An experimental test rig is used to simulate the models and the dynamics of the rotational system were captured using motion capture technology. The analytical and the experimental results demonstrate the behavior of this system and the effect of tank geometry, rate of migration of the center of mass induced by fuel transfer and fluid behavior inside the tanks. Further research is being carried out to compare the results obtained in this paper with existing propellant transfer systems. A detailed further analysis is required to develop a control system to actively stabilize this propellant storage and transfer system.


Authors: Vairamani M., Duraisamy V.V., Kulkarni M., Gangadharan S., Kirk D.R., Wilde M., Sathyanarayan D., Somanath N..

Affiliations: Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, University of Virginia, Pratt and Whitney, Florida Institute of Technology.

Publication: Space Flight Mechanics Meeting, 2018, 2018.
